evals.prompt: We have decided to add CSV export to reports in Quillmark Analytics. Before anybody builds it, I want us to nail down what it should do. Our requirements and backlog are attached, and so is a draft of ideas from an earlier chat.
evals.expected_output: Requirements are reconciled and only unresolved decisions are interviewed.
expectations: The specify skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent calls the document skill and reads the requirements, backlog, draft, and existing specifications before asking anything
Every applicable requirement (at least G1, G2, G3, and R2) is accounted for and none is silently dropped
The refine skill is called only for decisions still open and necessary for CSV export, not for settled requirements
The Excel, background export, and 30-day retention proposals stay marked as unresolved and are not treated as agreed behavior

evals.prompt: Use the specify skill for CSV export of reports. I settle everything now so please do not interview me: the export button appears for viewers who have access to the report; the file contains the visible columns and the current filter; users without export consent get a refusal message naming the missing consent; each export writes an audit entry; interface text is English and Dutch; a 10,000 row report must export within 5 seconds. Excel, background jobs, and retention are out of scope. The requirements are attached.
evals.expected_output: A specification is synthesized directly, with no interview, linked to the requirements.
expectations: The agent synthesizes directly and does not call the refine skill for questions the user already settled

A canonical specification is written in the repository with the problem and outcome, agreed behavior with edge cases, design and interfaces, acceptance and validation, requirement references, dependencies, and exclusions
The specification references G1, G2, G3, and R2 and states which behavior covers each
The out-of-scope items (Excel, background jobs, retention) are listed as exclusions, not as agreed behavior
The acceptance separates checks an agent can run (consent refusal, audit entry, the 5 second budget) from any human acceptance needed
An Agreement is recorded in the changelog for the authorized decisions, and the backlog and working state are updated

evals.prompt: Use the specify skill for CSV export. One open question is how the consent refusal should look: a modal, a toast, or an inline message under the button. I honestly cannot tell without seeing them. Requirements are attached.
evals.expected_output: A prototype is proposed and gated on approval, then used only within that scope.
expectations: The agent proposes a separately scoped prototype for the three refusal variants and asks for approval before building anything
The prototype skill is not called until the user approves, and then only within the approved scope
After the prototype, the agent records what its evidence establishes and what still needs production validation
The prototype's success alone is not claimed to establish production readiness

evals.prompt: Use the specify skill for CSV export, with the attached requirements. Simulate this: I tell you I cannot decide how long exported files may be kept, because legal has not answered, and that I do not want you to guess. Everything else is settled: viewers with access can export, the audit entry is written, text is bilingual.
evals.expected_output: The blocking decision stays explicit and open; progress is reported honestly.
expectations: The retention decision is recorded as an open blocker in the specification draft, not assumed or filled with a default
The agreed behavior is written without the retention rule, and the open item sits apart from agreed behavior
The final report lists the unresolved blocker and describes the result as partial progress, not as a complete specification
The agent does not record an Agreement in the changelog for the retention decision

evals.prompt: Use the specify skill to finish the CSV export scope; everything is settled and the specification is written. Give me the end-of-run report and say what I should do next. Nothing is authorized for any tracker; the scratch repository has no remote.
evals.expected_output: A complete report with canonical paths and next-step options, without running them or publishing.
expectations: The report names the canonical specification paths, the covered requirements, the agreements, any unresolved blockers, and the validation still needed
The next-step options offered are taskify, implement, or iterate, and the agent does not start any of them
No remote record is published or changed and the repository specification is stated to be the source of truth
The agent does not demand an exhaustive specification for future product work such as scheduled report emails

evals.prompt: Use the specify skill. The export-to-CSV capability is fully settled in this conversation. Write the specification.
evals.expected_output: The specification is synthesized without an interview, and the agent ends by offering taskify, implement, or iterate for the user to run.
expectations: The agent synthesizes the specification without re-asking settled decisions
The report lists the canonical paths, covered requirements, agreements, and blockers
The agent offers `/taskify`, `/implement`, or `/iterate` as the user's next move and does not start any of them

evals.prompt: The CSV export specification is approved and in the repository. Break it into tasks with explicit blocking dependencies that I can hand to different agents.
evals.expected_output: Decomposing agreed work is a taskify request.
expectations: The specify skill is not invoked and no decisions are re-opened
The agent uses the taskify skill (or names it) and produces a breakdown for approval

evals.prompt: I have ten ideas for the reports area: CSV export, scheduled emails, saved filters, a mobile view, comments, and five more. I cannot tell which one to build first. Help me choose.
evals.expected_output: Choosing among competing ideas is prioritize; specify works on one selected scope.
expectations: The specify skill is not invoked and no specification is written
The agent uses the prioritize skill (or names it) to decompose the ideas into outcomes and recommend one focus
